  obfuscation.base64_observation  [LOW]  OBSERVATION
    Inference   : 1 region(s) contain data that decodes cleanly as Base64.
    Confidence  : low — Base64 is a generic, ubiquitous encoding used constantly by benign software
                  (certificates, config blobs, telemetry, embedded assets) — its mere presence
                  carries no information about intent. Reported as an observation and never drives
                  the obfuscation score by itself; only a decoded PE header or shellcode bootstrap
                  pattern (see obfuscation.structural_payload) does.
    Facts: available — use --verbose to list
    Limitations:
      - IOC-style strings inside decoded content are a lead, not proof — see
        obfuscation.base64_observation facts / stomping-style string caveats.

  obfuscation.structural_payload  [HIGH]  DETECTION
    Inference   : Decoded/decompressed content from one or more obfuscation layers structurally
                  validates as a PE image.
    Confidence  : high — Unlike raw entropy/Base64/GZIP presence, this checks WHAT the decoded bytes
                  actually are: full PE structural validation (DOS/COFF/optional header + complete
                  section table). Encoding was only the delivery mechanism here — the payload itself
                  is the evidence.
    Facts: available — use --verbose to list
    Limitations:
      - Structural validation reduces but does not eliminate false positives from
        adversarially-crafted or coincidental byte sequences in high-entropy data.

  [ VERDICT ]  LIKELY — one structural indicator (sleep-mask decode or PE payload)  (1/2 — structural detections only; entropy/Base64/GZIP/shellcode-prefix are observations/leads, never a verdict by themselves)

  Use --verbose to expand region addresses, decoded content, and IOC strings.
